subject: Term extension & support-tier conversion — action items
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rachel Lin <r.lin@aperturehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 13 Nov 2025 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal proposal & support-tier conversion — Aperture Health (DEAL-2347)

Hi Rachel —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. As discussed, I'm sending a concise proposal to convert Aperture Health from the Standard support tier to our Premium SLA at renewal, plus the 20% capacity uplift you requested for Q1. Key points attached: renewal_summary_v2.pdf (high level) and SLA_addendum_draft.docx (legal draft).

What we'll cover if Aperture signs:
- 12-month term extension (starts 2026-01-01)
- Premium SLA: 99.95% uptime, 95th percentile latency SLO of 220ms for standard gen requests, tailored on-call escalation windows
- Dedicated burst capacity reservation: +20% committed GPU capacity for peak windows
- Onboarding: 4-week ops onramp with a joint runbook and two training sessions

Preliminary commercial notes (see pricing_term_sheet_v3.xlsx): one-time onboarding fee and a monthly uplift on committed usage. Ben is copied to confirm numbers; Evelyn will chime in on any contractual constraints.

Next steps I propose:
1) Rachel: confirm list of production endpoints and expected monthly token volumes so we can finalize pricing.
2) Ben: send final term pricing and crediting approach for on-call (we discussed a 50/50 split on critical incident credits).
3) Legal: if Aperture is comfortable, we can push the SLA_addendum to redlines and aim for a DocuSign send the week of 11/24.

If this all looks reasonable, I'll follow up with an ops onboarding checklist and timeline.

Best,
Logan Wright
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwoodinference.com
(415) 555-0142

Attachments: renewal_summary_v2.pdf, SLA_addendum_draft.docx, pricing_term_sheet_v3.xlsx

Logan —

Thanks for the clear summary. A few items from procurement and engineering before we proceed to legal:

- Can you confirm the 95th percentile latency SLO applies to our prod endpoints only and whether the 220ms target is for the cached (KV) path or end-to-end? We need end-to-end numbers for our compliance team.
- On-call credits: procurement wants the mechanism in writing (how credits are calculated per incident and how they apply against invoicing).
- Capacity uplift: we expect peak windows around 10–12 PT; can you confirm whether burst capacity is zonal or cross-region?

I can share our monthly token forecast once I validate with engineering (aiming to send by EOD Friday). Also looping in our procurement mailbox here.

Regards,
Rachel Lin
Head of Procurement, Aperture Health
r.lin@aperturehealth.com

Logan / Evelyn —

Pricing & credit mechanics (summary):

- Premium uplift: +18% monthly on committed usage (baseline committed units in pricing_term_sheet_v3.xlsx).
- One-time onboarding fee: $18,000 (covers joint runbook, two training sessions, priority ops support during 4-week ramp).
- Incident crediting: for Severity 1 incidents, we propose a credit equal to 5% of that month's committed spend per incident, capped at 20% / month. For S2, 2% per incident capped at 8% / month. Credits apply to the subsequent invoice.
- On-call credit split: 50/50 split for incidents where both vendors (Redwood and Aperture infra) contributed to a fault during the first 90 days of the ramp. After 90 days, standard SLAs apply and credits revert to the stated amounts.

Operational notes: burst capacity will be cross-region within the customer's primary region (us-west) — we will prioritize us-west availability and provide fallback in us-east if capacity constraints occur. That said, cross-region failover will have a different latency profile (we should call that out in the addendum).

I'll attach an ops onboarding checklist and the pricing sheet for the redline. Ben attached ops_onboarding_checklist.xlsx and pricing_term_sheet_v3.xlsx to this thread.

— Ben
Ben Carter

Ben — thanks for the clarity. A couple follow-ups from our engineering & compliance leads:

- End-to-end 95th percentile: can Redwood commit to 95th percentile end-to-end latency <= 300ms (prod endpoints, p95) for the first 90 days post-onboarding, with a remediation plan if we exceed that twice in a month? We'll accept slightly higher numbers during ramp if documented and paired with a remediation runbook.
- Incident credit wording: procurement suggests adding an explicit definition of 'incident contribution' (i.e., how we determine proportional responsibility). We can redline the addendum.
- DocuSign: once commercial & SLA language are mutually agreed, we'll expect a single DocuSign package for term extension + SLA addendum.

I'll send the token forecast in a separate email by EOD.
